name: Stanford Linear Collider
notes: The SLC used the SLAC linac itself as its accelerator, not as an injector ("Starting in 1983, extensive modifications and additions to the existing linac enabled it to simultaneously accelerate and collide 50 GeV electrons and positron bunches on a pulse-to-pulse basis", SLAC handbook page): see accelerator:slac-linac.

beam_energy.note: This is the SLC linac's quoted maximum per-beam energy, not the energy used for physics: to sit on the Z resonance the collider ran at cms/2 ~ 45.5-45.6 GeV per beam (cms energy ~91 GeV). The 50 GeV figure is sourced to Wikipedia only, so confidence is uncertain.
beam_energy.quote: an RF linear accelerator that accelerated electrons and positrons up to 50 GeV

cms_energy.locator: arXiv:hep-ex/0004026, section on the SLC beams (Ecm measured with energy spectrometers); arXiv PDF p. 4
cms_energy.note: Luminosity-weighted mean e⁺e⁻ centre-of-mass energy measured by the SLD at the SLC: 91.26 ± 0.03 GeV (1996 run) and 91.237 ± 0.029 GeV (1997-98 run, calibrated to the Z mass). The recorded value 91 GeV is these figures rounded to the nearest GeV (approx flag set); the collider ran at the Z resonance.
cms_energy.quote: The luminosity-weighted mean e+ e− center-of-mass energy (Ecm ) was measured with precision energy spectrometers [8] and was found to be 91.26±0.03 GeV for the 1996 run.

summary.plain: A particle collider at SLAC that smashed together beams of electrons and positrons tuned to the mass of the Z boson, letting physicists study that particle's properties with the SLD detector from 1989 to 1998.
summary.technical: Stanford Linear Collider: SLAC's linac accelerated electrons and positrons (up to 50 GeV per beam by design) around a single-pass arc to collide at the Z resonance (~91 GeV cms, ~45.5 GeV/beam), studied by the SLD detector, 1989-1998.
